title: PLS Nexus
shortDescription: The flagship AI-powered SaaS platform for entrepreneurs and small businesses — being built module by module, starting with Talent Intelligence.
longDescription: Rather than one monolithic build, PLS Nexus is being developed as a series of modules, each with its own repository and its own focused scope. PLS Nexus Talent Intelligence is the first of these modules — an AI resume-analysis backend — with its entity design and auth pattern intended to become the reusable template for every module that follows: workflow automation, CRM, analytics, and business management.
problem: Small teams stitch together a dozen separate tools to run their operations — AI assistants, workflow automation, CRM, analytics, communication, and productivity tools all live in different apps.

title: PLS Compress
shortDescription: A no-sign-up toolkit for shrinking images, shrinking PDFs, and merging PDFs — everything processed in memory through a Python backend, nothing stored after the response goes back.
longDescription: PLS Compress rebuilds a PDF's internal structure with pikepdf and, where it's safe to do so, re-encodes oversized embedded photos at a lower quality — page text is never touched, so documents stay sharp and stay searchable. Images are re-encoded through Pillow with a chosen format, quality, and optional width cap, with EXIF rotation respected. Every tool shows a before-and-after size comparison and percentage reduction before download. The frontend is server-rendered HTML with a single Jinja2 template and vanilla JS — no build step, no framework, so anyone can clone the repo and run it immediately.
problem: Shrinking a photo or a bloated PDF for email or upload usually means signing up for a web tool, and merging multiple PDFs into one is rarely free. PLS Compress needed no account and left nothing stored server-side.
features: Image compression (JPG/PNG/WEBP/BMP) with format, quality, and width controls
PDF compression that re-encodes oversized embedded images without touching page text
Merge 2-20 PDFs into one, in upload order
Before/after size comparison with percentage reduction
In-memory processing — no database, no persistence, nothing stored after the response

title: PLS QR
shortDescription: Turn a list of links or text into a batch of styled QR codes in seconds — paste a list or upload a CSV, export as a ZIP of PNGs or one printable PDF sheet.
longDescription: Making QR codes one at a time on a generic web tool is fine for a single link — it stops being fine the moment there's a real list behind it: a menu with twelve items, an event with fifty attendee badges, a warehouse full of product labels. PLS QR automates that repetitive step. Input is parsed into label/data pairs from pasted text or an uploaded CSV (recognizing data/value/url/link and label/name columns), each rendered as a styled QR code with a configurable error-correction level, then exported either as an in-memory ZIP of PNGs or laid out into a grid on printable PDF sheets via ReportLab.
problem: Bulk QR code generation for events, menus, or product labels usually means a paid tool or manually generating codes one by one.
features: Paste a list or upload a CSV (auto-detects label/data columns)
Custom code color, background color, and error-correction level
Export as a ZIP of individually labeled PNGs
Export as a printable PDF sheet (2-4 column grid, auto paginated)

title: PLS Snip
shortDescription: A no-sign-up URL shortener. Paste a long link, get a short one back, and check click stats later using a private management link — no account, no password.
longDescription: Creating a short link also returns a one-time management link built from a second, unrelated random token — the same trust model as an unlisted share link. Opening it later shows click count, creation/expiry dates, and last-clicked time, and lets you delete the link. Custom aliases are validated against a reserved-word list so a custom code can never collide with a real route, and links can be set to expire after 1, 7, 30, or 90 days, or never. Runs on a single SQLite file in WAL mode — no separate database server to install.
problem: Most URL shorteners require an account just to see basic click stats on a link you created thirty seconds ago.
features: Custom aliases (3-30 chars) or auto-generated short codes
Private, token-based management link — click count, created/expiry/last-clicked dates, delete
No account, no login — the management link itself is the access control
Reserved-word protection so custom aliases can't collide with real routes

title: PLS Crack
shortDescription: A no-sign-up code-breaking game. The server picks a hidden sequence of colors; you try to find it before you run out of attempts, using scored feedback to narrow it down.
longDescription: A classic code-breaking puzzle that genuinely needs a backend: if the secret code were generated in the browser it would sit in plain sight in the page's JavaScript, so the secret lives server-side and is only revealed once a game has actually ended. Starting a game creates an entry in an in-memory dictionary keyed by an unguessable token (secrets.token_urlsafe) — a capability rather than an identity, so there's nothing to sign up for. Scoring counts exact position-and-color matches first, then, from what's left, counts shared colors without double-counting any single peg — the part of this kind of puzzle that's easy to get subtly wrong when a color repeats, so it's covered by unit tests.
problem: A Mastermind-style guessing game can't be built as a purely client-side page without exposing the secret code in the page's own source.
features: Configurable code length (3-6), color count (4-8), and attempts (4-12)
Server-held secret, revealed only when the game ends
Peg-and-ring scored feedback per guess (exact-match vs. wrong-position)
Token-based game state — no login, no database, in-memory with automatic cleanup after inactivity

title: PLS Nigerian SMB Data Sanitizer
shortDescription: A production-grade Python data engineering pipeline for sanitizing and standardizing Nigerian SME transaction data — phone numbers, currency, dates, and duplicates, with a full quality report.
longDescription: This is the Community Edition, published as a free portfolio project, with a Pro Edition (larger example datasets, a dataset generator, a benchmark suite, and extended documentation) planned separately. The pipeline handles multi-encoding CSV ingestion (UTF-8, latin-1, cp1252) with automatic fallback, normalizes Nigerian phone numbers to E.164 format, strips Naira symbols and formatting from currency fields, standardizes mixed date formats to YYYY-MM-DD using fully vectorized pandas operations, and produces a per-field quality report after cleaning.
